problem: Image-goal navigation foundation models (GNM, ViNT, NoMaD) rely on massive pretraining and heavy compute, and still need costly in-domain adaptation to work reliably on a specific robot and environment. Training a small in-domain policy from scratch is hard because it needs diverse data under a tight real-world interaction budget.
motivation: If target-domain data collection is unavoidable for a given platform, rapid purely in-domain learning could be a cheaper route to deployment than large-scale pretraining or human demonstrations. Offline RL can learn from static, unlabeled exploration data, but it has mostly been evaluated in simulation, and its performance depends heavily on dataset coverage.
key_idea: Collect 1-2 hours of autonomous, unlabeled RGB and velocity data with temporally correlated but action-uniform 'pink uniform' noise, then train a small goal-conditioned TD3+BC policy on frozen DINOv3 features with hindsight goal relabeling, all on a laptop in under two hours.
insight: Dataset coverage is the bottleneck. Pink uniform noise gives the highest state, action and joint entropy, and in real-world 1h data it reaches 43% SR versus 30% for pink Gaussian and 15% for white uniform. Performance scales strongly with data (Standard scene SR 43% to 88% from 1h to 2h with ViT-S). A compact ViT-S encoder is nearly as good as ViT-L, and FQE scores correlate with true success (Spearman 0.91), so checkpoints can be selected offline without real-world trials.
method: Pink uniform noise exploration: generate 1/f (beta=1) pink noise via inverse FFT, then apply the Gaussian CDF (probability integral transform) and rescale to the action range. This keeps temporal correlation and gives uniform action coverage, including the extremes of the control range.
Frozen DINOv3 encoder: extracts normalized features from 448x784 RGB (ViT-S or ViT-L distilled), so no visual encoder is trained.

Valid goal filtering by spatial standard deviation (SSD): the SSD of center-cropped DINOv3 patch embeddings must exceed 0.02, which removes uninformative observations (e.g. close to a wall) from the goal set.

State and reward design: the state stacks the features of 4 consecutive frames. The reward is sparse, 1 when the mean cosine similarity between the 4 frames and the goal is at least 0.8, and this also terminates the episode.
Hindsight goal relabeling: geometric future sampling mixed 0.5/0.5 with global uniform sampling from the valid goal set for critic training; uniform goals only for actor training.
Goal-conditioned TD3+BC: clipped double-Q critics with a BC-regularized actor (lambda=0.001), trained for 50k steps with batch size 1024 on the laptop GPU.
Fitted Q-Evaluation model selection: an independent Q-network evaluates each saved checkpoint offline, and the highest-FQE checkpoint is deployed.

setting.backbone: Frozen DINOv3 (ViT-S / ViT-L distilled) features + small TD3+BC actor-critic MLP policy trained from scratch
setting.model_size: 2M trainable policy params (DINOv3 ViT-S/L encoder frozen)
setting.training_data: 1 h or 2 h of autonomously collected in-domain RGB + velocity command data per environment, with no human demonstrations or pretraining on navigation data
setting.observation: monocular RGB (720x1280 resized to 448x784), 4-frame stack of DINOv3 features; LiDAR only for collision stop, not a policy input
setting.action_space: continuous velocity [vx, vy, wz] in [-1,1]^3 at 2 Hz, smoothed to 20 Hz
setting.simulator: MuJoCo (modified OGBench PointMaze) for exploration and FQE analysis; real-world indoor rooms
setting.privileged: none at test time (goal image only); ground-truth coordinates are used only for the simulation entropy metrics; success is judged by a similarity proxy (0.75) plus manual review

numbers_note: Results are on the authors' own real-world indoor scenes, not a standard benchmark. Simulation results (success vs. data budget, entropy, FQE correlation of 0.91) are given only in figures. The Standard-scene ViT-L 1h and 2h rows and other 1h rows are omitted for space, but are in Table 1. Robustness table: Go2 static SR 100 / dynamic SR 100; Limo static SR 92 / dynamic SR 88 (5 goals, Standard scene, 2h data).
results: With just 1 h of in-domain data, MINav (ViT-S) reaches 73% SR in the Simple room versus 18% (NoMaD), 8% (ViT NT), 9% (GNM) for zero-shot foundation models. With 2 h it reaches 88-100% SR in the Simple and Standard rooms and up to 85% (ViT-L) in the Complex room, where the best baseline, GNM, gets 25%. The full pipeline runs in 85-111 min for the 1 h setting on an RTX 5070 laptop.
limitations: Baselines are zero-shot foundation models, not adapted or fine-tuned in-domain, so the comparison is deployment-oriented rather than adaptation-matched.

Evaluated only in three small indoor scenes on one main robot (Go2) plus a Limo. The Complex scene is still hard for 1h data (25-38% SR). Success uses a feature-similarity proxy with manual verification, and SPL cannot be computed because path lengths are unavailable.
Needs a fresh 1-2 h data collection per environment and depends on frozen DINOv3 features and a similarity-based reward; no cross-environment generalization.
compares_to: White / Pink Gaussian / OU noise exploration
